periodos.nombre: Iron Age II — Edomite fortress conquered by Amaziah

descripcion_geo: Edomite fortress excavated in rock ('sela' literally means 'rock' or 'rock' in Hebrew), in mountainous terrain with difficult access to the south of the Salt Sea, identified by much of the tradition with the region where the Nabataean city of Petra would later be developed.
clima: Semi-arid mountain — hot, dry summers, cold winters, typical of the Edom highlands.
recursos: Natural fortification in rock that is difficult to access
Defensive position in mountainous Edomite terrain
importancia_estrategica: Shelah is the scene of one of the most significant military victories of Judah over Edom: its conquest by Amaziah, followed by the mass execution of Edomite prisoners thrown from the rock, marks an episode of extreme violence that illustrates the intensity of the conflict between both neighboring kingdoms during the divided monarchy.

otros_habitantes.descripcion: Original population of the fortress of Shela, part of the kingdom of Edom, conquered by Amaziah of Judah in his military campaign against this neighboring town.
Judah military forces conquer Shelah and execute a massive number of Edomite prisoners by throwing them from the top of the rock.

historias.titulo: Amaziah conquers Shelah and renames her Jocteel
historias.descripcion: After defeating ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, Amaziah of Judah marches against Shelah, captures her and gives her the name Jocteel, which she retains to the time of the biblical account, consolidating one of the few significant military victories of Judah recorded during this period.

historias.titulo: Ten thousand Edomite prisoners are thrown from the rock
historias.descripcion: According to the chronicler's account, in addition to the ten thousand killed in battle, Amaziah captures another ten thousand living Edomites, takes them to the top of the rock of Shelah and throws them off the cliff from there, all of them dying destroyed, an episode of extreme brutality that the text records without explicit condemnation but that contrasts with the subsequent moral fall of Amaziah for idolizing the captured Edomite gods.

historias.titulo: Messengers sent from Shela at the oracle of Isaiah
historias.descripcion: The prophet Isaiah refers to messengers sent 'from Shelah into the wilderness' in connection with an oracle of protection for Moab's fugitives, linking the Edomite stronghold with the geography of the region's political and prophetic movements.

personajes.descripcion: He conquers the Edomite fortress of Shelah after a previous military victory against Edom, an episode that represents the climax of his militarily successful reign, before his subsequent fall into idolatry that would lead to the deterioration of his reign.
Ten thousand men captured alive after the conquest of Sela, executed by falling off the rock, an episode of extreme violence that marks the conflict between Judah and Edom during this period.
He mentions Shela as a geographical point of reference in his oracle on Moab, connecting the Edomite fortress with the movements of fugitives and messengers in the region.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Shela is the scene of one of the most extreme episodes of war violence narrated without explicit condemnation in the chronicle text, although the immediate subsequent context—the apostasy of Amaziah by adopting the cult of the captured Edomite gods—suggests an implicit theological connection between the military victory and the subsequent spiritual fall of the king, a recurring pattern in Deuteronomist theology where excessive military success frequently precedes religious arrogance.

mitos.nombre: Shelah's victory and Amaziah's subsequent apostasy

judaismo.fuente_secundaria: Comentario rabínico tradicional sobre la conexión entre el éxito militar de Amasías en Sela y su posterior idolatría con los dioses edomitas capturados
judaismo.descripcion: Jewish tradition carefully observes the contrast between Amaziah's military victory at Shelah and his later inexplicable decision to worship the same Edomite gods who had not been able to save his people from defeat, interpreting this episode as a paradigmatic warning about how military success can generate arrogance that leads directly to religious apostasy.
judaismo.significado_teologico: Amaziah's victory-apostasy sequence illustrates the theological danger of attributing military success to wrong sources, leading to the idolatry of precisely the defeated gods.
